root_cause.title: Non-atomic check-revoke in rotate() causes false TokenReuseDetected → revokeFamily() wipes winner's fresh token
root_cause.explanation: Two concurrent POST /auth/refresh requests arrive with the same rt cookie. Both call findByHash() synchronously (SQLite) and both read the same row with revoked_at=null before either has written. The first request proceeds: it calls revoke(row.id) then inserts a fresh token. The second request — which resumed after an await boundary in the event loop — re-reads the same token hash from the DB and now sees revoked_at IS set (written by the first request). It interprets this as token theft/reuse and calls revokeFamily(), marking the entire family as revoked. The authMiddleware then rejects the winner's valid access token with 401 because isFamilyRevoked() returns true for that family.

causal_chain.what: Two simultaneous POST /auth/refresh requests with identical rt cookie, no concurrency guard at the controller level.
Both requests enter rotate(). Both call findByHash(sha256(oldToken)) and both read row.revoked_at=null. Both pass the reuse check (line 56).
First request calls repo.revoke(row.id) at line 60, marking the token row as revoked. It then inserts a new token and returns a fresh access token.

Second request re-reads the same row (after an await boundary) and sees revoked_at IS now set. It incorrectly concludes token reuse is happening and calls revokeFamily(row.family_id), which marks token_families.revoked_at AND revokes all refresh_tokens in that family.
authMiddleware calls isFamilyRevoked(fid) on the winner's valid access token JWT. Returns true. /me responds 401. User is logged out.

hypotheses.statement: Non-atomic read-then-revoke in rotate() allows the losing concurrent request to falsely detect token reuse and call revokeFamily(), invalidating the winner's fresh access token.

fix_direction.summary: Replace the read-check-revoke sequence in rotate() with an atomic UPDATE ... WHERE revoked_at IS NULL on the refresh_tokens row. If the UPDATE affects 0 rows, the token was already claimed by a concurrent request — treat it as InvalidToken (not TokenReuseDetected / not revokeFamily). Only call revokeFamily() when a token that was provably already revoked is presented, i.e. when findByHash finds a row with revoked_at already set at the initial read. This eliminates the false-positive reuse detection triggered by legitimate concurrent refresh.
fix_direction.regression_test_idea: Two concurrent POST /auth/refresh with same rt cookie → exactly one returns 200 with accessToken → GET /me with that token returns 200. Already captured in the frozen repro test.
